clue.text: £50 needed to cover current drink

indicators.note: to cover says the money pieces sit either side of the symbol for current, holding it

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty
a quid is British slang for one pound sterling
I is the physics symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: Someone has to pay fifty pounds for the drink they are having right now.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces are written in the order L then QUID, and 'to cover' puts I between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Any fluid you can swallow is a drink, so the noun for something runny serves here.

clue.text: Officer seizing old quarter of fishing port

indicators.note: seizing means the officer's abbreviation grips the other pieces between its letters

parts.note: LT is the abbreviation for lieutenant
west is one of the four quarters of the compass
taken as written

explanation.surface: An officer takes over the old district of a fishing town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quarter' looks like a district of the town but is a compass point. Lowestoft is a fishing port in Suffolk, on England's east coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Lowestoft is a Suffolk town long known for its herring fleet, a fishing port.

clue.text: Angry disagreement regarding arrow

definitions.meaning: a square-headed bolt fired from a crossbow

explanation.definitionFit: A quarrel is both a heated argument and the short bolt shot from a crossbow.

clue.text: Doing porridge at home, then beginning to steam fish

parts.note: in means at home, as in staying in

indicators.note: beginning to says only the first letter of the next word is used

parts.note: the ide is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: At home someone is about to steam fish, perhaps with porridge to follow.
explanation.walkthrough: Porridge is British slang for a prison sentence, so someone doing porridge is serving time.
explanation.definitionFit: Being inside is slang for being in prison, which is what serving a sentence means.

clue.text: Neat-sounding barrel used by a weaver?

indicators.note: sounding says only the pronunciation of the word for neat is wanted

parts.note: neat is an old word for cattle, so a bull is a neat
to barrel along is to rush at speed

explanation.surface: Someone describes a tidy-sounding cask that a cloth-maker uses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Neat' looks like tidy, but it is the old word for an ox; BULL said aloud gives BUL. The question mark flags that the definition is an example: rushes are woven into mats and baskets.
explanation.definitionFit: Marsh reeds of this kind are woven into baskets, mats and chair seats, so a weaver of rush work uses them.

clue.text: Moorish lad carrying goods?

indicators.note: carrying means the boy holds the other piece inside him

parts.note: a lad is a boy
G is short for good, so two of them make goods

explanation.surface: A Moorish boy carries some merchandise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moorish' looks like the North African people, but it means like a moor: wet and marshy.
explanation.definitionFit: Moorland is often marshy and waterlogged, so like a moor means soggy underfoot.

clue.text: Left with evangelist for Durham Cathedral, say

parts.note: and can mean with, as in fish and chips
Mark is one of the four gospel writers

explanation.surface: Someone sets off with a gospel writer to see Durham Cathedral.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' marks the definition as an example: Durham Cathedral is a famous building in northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: A prominent, easily recognised building like a great cathedral is a landmark.

clue.text: Naval commander supports place of learning — he's fabulous!

indicators.note: in a down clue, supports means the following pieces sit under the place of learning

parts.note: uni is short for university
CO is short for commanding officer
RN is the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: A naval commander backs a college, and is applauded as a marvellous chap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fabulous' looks like praise but means belonging to fable.
explanation.definitionFit: A unicorn is a mythical beast of legend, so it is literally a creature of fable.

clue.text: Old PM sets scene for witches encounter with Macbeth

definitions.meaning: Edward ... was British prime minister from 1970 to 1974

definitions.text: scene for witches encounter with Macbeth
definitions.meaning: in Shakespeare's play the three witches meet Macbeth on a blasted moor

explanation.definitionFit: Edward Heath was a Conservative prime minister, and a stretch of open moorland is where the witches meet Macbeth.

clue.text: Canvas old woman at auction talked of

indicators.note: talked of says the pieces are spoken, and their sound gives the spelling

parts.note: ma is a familiar word for mother, one's old woman; something at auction is in sale

explanation.surface: Someone discusses a painting their mother put up at auction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Canvas' looks like a painting, but it means sailcloth: the principal sail of a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Sails are made of canvas, and sailors call a ship's sails its canvas, so the main one fits.

clue.text: Wife criticises shawls

parts.note: to rap someone is to rebuke or criticise them

explanation.surface: A wife finds fault with some shawls.
explanation.definitionFit: Shawls are garments draped around the shoulders, which are called wraps.

clue.text: A top priority to have leader deposed in a state

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the leader of the word is deposed, so its opening letter is removed

parts.note: something of top priority is urgent
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: In some country, removing the leader has become the most pressing matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader deposed' takes the U off URGENT, leaving RGENT; 'state' means a nation, not a condition.
explanation.definitionFit: Argentina is a South American country, and state is a common word for a nation.

clue.text: Harshness of jazz piano style about to invade New York

parts.note: stride is a jazz piano style with a leaping left hand

indicators.note: to invade means the small piece pushes into the abbreviation for the city

parts.note: C is short for circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: A critic complains of the harsh tone of a jazz piano style about to hit New York.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'concerning' but gives the abbreviation for circa; 'to invade' puts it inside the city's initials.
explanation.definitionFit: Stridency is loud harshness of sound or manner, the quality of being grating.

clue.text: Move aimlessly, being Low Church

parts.note: to low is to moo, as cattle do

explanation.surface: Someone drifts about aimlessly, being a member of the Low Church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Low Church' is a real phrase for the evangelical wing of the Church of England, which hides the cow's call.
explanation.definitionFit: To mooch is to wander about idly with no particular purpose.

clue.text: Give the glad eye, monster having left for run

indicators.note: having left for run means the letter for left replaces the letter for run in the word

parts.note: an ogre is a monster of folk tales
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A monster, having fled instead of running, gives someone a flirtatious look.
explanation.walkthrough: In OGRE the R (run) is replaced by L (left).
explanation.definitionFit: To ogle is to look at someone with obvious desire, giving them the glad eye.

clue.text: Aimless movements air force units accept with hesitation

indicators.note: accept says the air force units take the other pieces inside them

parts.note: a wing is an air force formation
and can mean with, as in bread and butter
er is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: Air force squadrons go along with some dithering about where to fly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' gives a conjunction rather than linking, and 'accept' has the air force units take the rest inside them.
explanation.definitionFit: Wanderings are journeys or roamings without a fixed course or goal.

clue.text: Loathing inspector's condition, second son has a drop

indicators.note: in a down clue, has a drop says that letter falls lower in the word

parts.note: DI is a detective inspector, so inspector's gives DI plus S
a state is a condition
S is short for son, and here it is the second of the two in the word

explanation.surface: An inspector's state of mind worsens as a second son takes to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: In DISSTATE the second S drops two places, giving the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Distaste is strong dislike or aversion, close to loathing.

clue.text: One enters output in a book of verse

definitions.text: One enters output in a book of verse

parts.words: One enters output in a book of verse
parts.note: a poet who writes fourteen-line poems puts his work into a collection of verse

explanation.definitionFit: A writer of fourteen-line poems produces work that goes into collections of verse.

clue.text: Don't cook enough game at first, being in inferior position

parts.note: to underdo food is to cook it too little

indicators.note: at first says only the opening letter of game is used

explanation.surface: A cook who leaves game too rare starts off at a disadvantage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being' is a noun here, a creature, so the definition reads as one who is placed lower.
explanation.definitionFit: An underdog is the party expected to lose, a creature in the weaker position.

clue.text: Unskilled soldiers made fewer advances

parts.note: the TA, Territorial Army, is Britain's reserve force of part-time soldiers
to make fewer advances, as in loans, is to have lent less

explanation.surface: Some soldiers lacking ability made less progress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'advances' looks like military progress but means loans: made fewer advances is lent less.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone untalented has no special gifts, so lacks skill.

clue.text: Characters providing digs?

definitions.meaning: people who rent out rooms; digs is British slang for lodgings

explanation.definitionFit: Alphabet symbols are written characters, and landlords who let rooms are those who let.

clue.text: Symbol of noble once, one sent to the front?

indicators.note: sent to the front says the letter for one is moved to the start of the word

parts.note: a noble was an old English gold coin
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A nobleman of old was once a symbol, and someone was sent to the battle front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'noble' looks like an aristocrat but is the medieval gold coin; moving its I to the front turns COIN into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An icon is an image or emblem standing for something, a symbol.

clue.text: Accommodation in fighters — and for fighters once

definitions.meaning: the pilot's compartment in a fighter plane
an arena where gamecocks were set to fight before the sport was banned

explanation.definitionFit: The pilot sits in a fighter plane's cabin, and cockfights were staged in a sunken ring.

clue.text: Like maladroit people left in Paris

definitions.meaning: awkward and tactless, as clumsy people are

explanation.definitionFit: Clumsy, socially awkward people are awkward in manner, and the French word for left gives the same spelling.

clue.text: Turner's part of mill at Henley

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A painter by the name of Turner owned a share of a mill at Henley.
explanation.walkthrough: Turner looks like the painter, but a turner is a woodworker, and the definition is possessive: the tool is the turner's.
explanation.definitionFit: A turner shapes wood or metal by spinning it on a lathe, so the machine is the turner's.

clue.text: Miss Leeds's first worthless fellow

parts.note: to miss something is to lose it

indicators.note: first says only the opening letter of Leeds is taken

explanation.surface: A Leeds lady's first boyfriend was a good-for-nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Miss' looks like a young woman, but it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A losel is an archaic word for a scoundrel or good-for-nothing.

clue.text: Landslide engendered by hail, trapping man by church

indicators.note: trapping means the greeting holds the other pieces inside it

parts.note: ave is Latin for hail, a greeting
Alan is a man's name

explanation.surface: A landslide set off by a hailstorm traps a man beside a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hail' looks like the weather but is the Latin greeting; 'trapping' puts the man and church inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An avalanche is a mass of snow or rock sliding down a mountain, a landslide.

clue.text: With no one to see, sweet Molly goes topless

indicators.note: goes topless means the first letter of the surname is removed

parts.note: sweet Molly Malone is the fishmonger of the Dublin song

explanation.surface: With nobody watching, sweet Molly strips off her top.
explanation.walkthrough: Molly Malone is the heroine of the Irish song Cockles and Mussels: 'sweet Molly Malone'.
explanation.definitionFit: Being solitary means having nobody else around to see you.

clue.text: New depot, base for building vessel

indicators.note: New says the letters are made into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A new depot is the base for building a boat.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram takes the letters of both depot and base together.
explanation.definitionFit: A speedboat is a fast motor boat, a kind of vessel.

clue.text: Manage to enclose small thicket

indicators.note: to enclose says the word for manage holds the letter inside it

parts.note: to cope is to manage

explanation.surface: Someone manages to fence in a little thicket.
explanation.walkthrough: S goes inside COPE after its P.
explanation.definitionFit: A copse is a small group of trees, a thicket or spinney.

clue.text: Way to keep back fuel for making pasta

indicators.note: to keep says the word for way holds the other piece inside it

parts.note: a lane is a way or road

indicators.note: back says the word for fuel is read from right to left

parts.note: gas is a fuel

explanation.surface: Someone has a way of keeping fuel in reserve for cooking pasta.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns the fuel round, and 'to keep' puts it inside the word for way; 'for making' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Lasagne is a kind of pasta made in broad flat sheets.

clue.text: Punter's cap

definitions.meaning: a punter is one who bets, so here the clue says a punter is one
to cap something is to outdo or improve on it

explanation.definitionFit: One who places bets is a bettor, also spelt this way; and capping something means surpassing it.
